pct.$comment: Here the `primary` ramp goes UP (lighter on hover/active), the opposite of the light theme. The reason is measurable, not aesthetic: in the dark theme `on-primary` is DARK, so darkening the background drives the label's contrast down instead of up — that once gave 3.45:1 on hover and 2.66:1 on active, below AA, with a green build. The same token is also text on a dark surface (the outline variant's label), and that needs a light step: blue.500 on `surface-100` gave 3.98:1.

hero-text.$comment: The gradient as TEXT, lifted for the dark ground. The surface stops (`hero`, `hero-via`, `hero-to`) are NOT overridden here on purpose — the brand's gradient is the same blue on both themes, and it is only the word cut out of it that has to move: 7.02, 6.56 and 7.35 against `surface`, where the unlifted stops read 3.45, 3.13 and 3.33.

pct.$comment-tones: The dark theme’s three, one step up the same ramps for the same reason every other colour here goes up: the ground lightens a colour by standing dark under it. Measured on `slate.900`: 10.25:1, 10.69:1 and 7.02:1. The rest of the note stands with the light theme’s — the three colours a tone needs beside `danger`, which the skin has had since the badge. They paint an ICON first and a fill second, because a tone that is only a colour is a state carried by colour alone (`req-a11y-forced-colors`, plan 4.14) — the drawing is the channel that survives a forced palette and a reader who cannot tell red from green. No `on-` pair for any of them: nothing in this library sets text on a toned background yet, and a declared-and-unused pair looks like coverage that does not exist (the note above `danger` records what that cost the last time).
pct.$comment-info: Info is the brand blue, and deliberately the same value as `primary`: an informational message is not an alarm, the skin has exactly one calm accent, and a fourth hue invented for it would be a colour with no meaning behind it. The name is separate because the ROLE is — a theme that recolours its brand should not have to think about what that does to a message.
pct.$comment-scrim: The veil, and here it has to be the ramp's endpoint rather than `slate.900`: the dark theme's page IS `slate.900`, so a veil of the same step would dim it by nothing at all. How translucent it is, and how far the page behind it is blurred, are the component's two other tokens — all three are the skin's to set.
pct.$comment-surface-inverse: The surface that answers the page rather than joining it — dark on a light theme and light on a dark one. It exists for the annotation kind of panel (the tooltip is the first): a surface a reader is meant to notice for a moment and then stop seeing, which the ordinary `surface` cannot be, being what the page is made of. The `on-` pair is not decoration here — an inverted surface is the one place where reaching for `pct.text` by reflex paints text the same colour as the box it stands in.
